primary_meaning: the Holy Spirit (His anointing, presence, empowerment, and illumination)
primary_basis: 1 Samuel 16:13 (anointing of David with oil accompanied by the Spirit of the Lord)
Isaiah 61:1 and Luke 4:18 (Spirit of the Lord anoints for ministry)
Acts 10:38 (God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power)
Zechariah 4:1-14 (oil flowing to the lampstand, interpreted as 'not by might nor by power but by my Spirit')
Matthew 25:1-13 (oil in the virgins' lamps commonly read as the Holy Spirit or His sustaining presence)

basis: James 5:14-15 (elders anoint the sick with oil)
Mark 6:13 (disciples anoint many sick with oil)
Luke 10:34 (oil used medicinally by the Good Samaritan)
Isaiah 61:3 (oil of joy instead of mourning)

alternatives.meaning: consecration / setting apart for sacred office or service
basis: Exodus 30:22-33 (holy anointing oil for tabernacle and priests)
1 Kings 1:39 and 19:16 (anointing of kings and prophets)

alternatives.meaning: readiness, vigilance, or personal spiritual preparation (distinct from the Spirit Himself)
basis: Matthew 25:1-13 (oil as the resource that keeps the lamp burning)

notes: Across patristic, Reformation, evangelical, and modern biblical-theological sources the dominant symbolic assignment of oil (especially olive oil used in anointing) is the Holy Spirit; other associations (healing, joy, consecration) are widely recognized but secondary or derivative of the Spirit motif rather than competing primaries.
